page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor featuring an x86_64 architecture with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core. Memory provision stands at 256.0 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities include 48 MB of L3 cache, instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (with VNNI support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 32 Gbps. The instance provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and contains no hardware GPUs.

Benchmark data reflects strong multi-threaded execution balanced by mid-tier single-threaded output. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieves top-quartile performance, including a stress-ng multi-core result of 62,017.14, a PassMark CPU score of 55,401.5, a Geekbench multi-core score of 16,705.0, and 288.7 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Targeted tests show strong marks in code compilation (Geekbench clang score of 40,694.0), ray tracing (57,014.0), PassMark encryption (50,307.65), and PassMark database operations (25,157.94). Memory tests register top-quartile PassMark scores (2,774.99) alongside moderate uncached memory bandwidth of 169.75 GB/sec read and 71.23 GB/sec write. Single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core (1,603.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (27.93 GB/sec), sit consistently in the middle 50% tier.

The 64-vCPU density yields favorable cost efficiency for horizontal, high-throughput computational workloads that scale across threads rather than relying on peak single-core clock speeds. Tradeoffs include the lack of integrated local NVMe storage and average single-thread performance, which limits responsiveness for latency-sensitive, unparallelized jobs. Small-scale CPU-driven inference runs effectively due to AVX-512 VNNI support, delivering 2,432.91 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models, but larger models show moderate performance without dedicated acceleration. Workload fit includes enterprise microservices, continuous integration build clusters, parallel compilation pipelines, and relational or distributed databases paired with external network volumes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7.16xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance equipped with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor, paired with 256.0 GB of memory and a 32 Gbps network baseline. Running under the KVM hypervisor, it features AVX-512 VNNI instructions but includes no bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile performance in multi-threaded tasks—evidenced by strong multi-core PassMark, Geekbench, and database operation scores—contrasted with mid-tier single-core results. The absence of local NVMe storage makes external storage attachment necessary. This hardware profile provides high compute density, making it well-suited for enterprise application serving, large-scale software compilation, distributed databases, and high-concurrency microservices.
